This is open, and cannot be resolved with a finite computation.
Give an asymptotic formula for the number of $k\times n$ Latin rectangles.
#725: [Er81]
combinatorics
Erdős and Kaplansky [ErKa46] proved the count is\[\sim e^{-\binom{k}{2}}(n!)^k\]when $k=o((\log n)^{3/2-\epsilon})$. Yamamoto [Ya51] extended this to $k\leq n^{1/3-o(1)}$.
The count of such Latin rectangles is A001009 in the OEIS.
Additional thanks to: Ralf Stephan

 The page should be updated to include the later result of Godsil and McKay (1990). If $L_{k,n}$ denotes the unrestricted number of $k\times n$ Latin rectangles on symbols $[n]$, they proved that, as $n\to\infty$ with $k=o(n^{6/7})$,
$$L_{k,n}\sim (n!)^k\left(\frac{(n)_k}{n^k}\right)^n\left(1-\frac{k}{n}\right)^{-n/2}e^{-k/2},$$
where $(n)_k=n(n-1)\cdots(n-k+1)$. This substantially extends the earlier results of Erdos-Kaplansky and Yamamoto.
It's probably also worth clarifying that OEIS A001009 is not the unrestricted count $L_{k,n}$. It records the reduced/normalised counts $R_{k,n}$ (ie. with the first row and first column fixed).

A partial proof 
claimed by Eric Li (using GPT-5.6 Sol Pro, Codex).
 Summary:
 The paper partially solves Erdős Problem 725 by proving that the number $ L_{k,n} $ of ordered $ k\times n $ Latin rectangles obeys the Godsil–McKay asymptotic
$$(n!)^k\Bigl(\frac{(n)_k}{n^k}\Bigr)^n\Bigl(1-\frac{k}{n}\Bigr)^{-n/2}e^{-k/2}$$
for every $ k=o(n) $, extending the earlier range $ k=o(n^{6/7}) $. A refined normalisation $ \widetilde A_{k,n} $ satisfies $ \log(L_{k,n}/\widetilde A_{k,n})=O(k^2/n^2) $ uniformly on any sublinear range.
The proof combines a permanent asymptotic for matrices close to the all-ones matrix (via a Gamma representation and cluster expansion isolating cycles) with a path-switching argument that controls residual second-moment statistics, then multiplies the resulting one-row extension ratios.
 Notes:
 This partial proof has been formally verified in Lean.
